items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: we had this trumpet player from New Orleans that had spent years in Vegas, Louis Prima... Four trumpets at the same time on stage

ctx.x: And then you had to follow him. They loved him there. So that, one of the bosses would send -- or do it themselves, see what Earl would do, because Earl would break down his drums. That's a modern term, tear down his drums. And pawn them so he'd get enough money. And they'd follow him and get the pawn tickets, and redeem them there, and he'd be working -- you know he'd been working . But he'd just get so drunk, that this one night, Dave T ough was visiting. And it was early in the evening. Earl was upstairs…

So they got Dave to sit in. After one set, they went up and got Earl. And they says, Dave is drunker than you are, come on down and finish the evening. But this -- one time I looked down at the bandstand, and we had Paul , we had Martie Marcella, we had this trumpet player from New Orleans that had spent years in Vegas, Louis Prima, and William . Four trumpets at the same time on stage, with Pee Wee used to come in all the time and sit in there.
It was a great place to sit in, it was a great place to drink and play music. They charged us five cents for a shot of gin.
